audit_findings.title: Post-FY2025 acquisition perimeter is missing from the earnings anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified OE effect; filed Gleamer purchase consideration was $264.1 million, including $255.5 million upfront and $8.6 million contingent consideration
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge reflects acquisition cash, debt and liabilities as of June 30, 2026, while OE and the associated interest burden remain anchored to the pre-acquisition FY2025 perimeter.
audit_findings.evidence: On March 2, 2026, the Company completed the acquisition of all of the outstanding shares of Gleamer SAS and its subsidiaries.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch. Gleamer's $264.1 million consideration exceeds the modeled $167 million bear equity value, so the omitted business and financing effects are reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation. Direction cannot be established because the acquired earnings, integration costs and incremental interest could collectively increase or decrease OE.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild OE through June 30, 2026 on a pro forma current-perimeter basis, including Gleamer earnings, integration costs, working capital, capex, acquired liabilities, contingent consideration and financing interest; alternatively rerun using a pre-acquisition bridge.

audit_findings.title: Parent earnings are mixed with consolidated cash flows and assets despite material NCI
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified valuation effect; filed NCI income was $35.699 million in 2025, and NCI equity was $265.996 million at December 31, 2025 and $297.959 million at June 30, 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Parent-attributable income is combined with consolidated D&A, working capital, capex and bridge cash that include portions economically belonging to noncontrolling owners.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, our consolidated subsidiaries operated 368 imaging centers of which 101 were not wholly-owned and thus a portion of their operating results were attributable to noncontrolling interests.
audit_findings.explanation: The inconsistent ownership basis is demonstrated, although the net correction is unresolved. NCI equity exceeds the $167 million bear equity value, and 2025 NCI income equals 64% of the absolute $55.6 million OE anchor. Including NCI cash and add-backs can overstate parent value, while charging all consolidated capex can understate it, so the direction is mixed.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a parent-economic-interest OE and cash bridge by allocating D&A, working capital, capex, lease cash flows and cash for each partially owned subsidiary; alternatively use fully consolidated OE and deduct a separately supported NCI value.

audit_findings.title: Unpaid acquisition consideration may be an undeducted claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $36.0 million filed at December 31, 2025; separately itemized June 30, 2026 contingent liabilities total $22.844 million, or $0.28 per valuation share
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash-settled holdbacks and contingent consideration should reduce the equity bridge, while stock-settled obligations should increase diluted shares.
audit_findings.evidence: These acquisitions included holdbacks and other liabilities totaling $ 36.0 million that we had not paid for as of December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge's exclusion of acquisition liabilities is a demonstrated structural omission, although the current cash-versus-stock split and remaining holdbacks are unresolved. The specifically itemized June liabilities equal 13.7% of the $167 million bear equity value but only $0.28 per share, versus a $71.64 gap between the $73.71 market price and the highest modeled value of $2.07. Even the filed $36.0 million year-end amount is only $0.45 per valuation share, so the supplied amounts cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every June 30 holdback and contingent liability to subsequent settlements; deduct the cash-settled balance and add shares for stock-settled obligations, while avoiding double counting amounts already paid or issued.

audit_findings.title: The iCAD share issuance is matched to only a partial year of acquired earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed all-stock purchase consideration was $110.7 million
audit_findings.mechanism: The diluted-share denominator reflects acquisition shares and replacement options, but the OE anchor includes only post-July 17, 2025 operating results and transaction or integration effects.
audit_findings.evidence: On July 17, 2025, we completed the acquisition of all of the outstanding equity interests of iCAD, Inc. (“iCAD”), a global leader in AI-powered breast health solutions.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated, but the record does not isolate iCAD's full-year OE contribution. Missing recurring losses would overstate value, while temporary integration costs or omitted profitable months could understate it. The $110.7 million transaction establishes meaningful perimeter scale but does not quantify the sustainable OE correction.
audit_findings.action: Obtain iCAD's full-year pro forma income and cash-flow schedules, separate recurring operations from transaction and integration costs, calculate maintenance capex and working capital, confirm replacement-option dilution, and rerun OE on the matched perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Joint-venture support contributions may be omitted from owner cash requirements
audit_findings.magnitude: $20.5 million contributed in 2025 versus $1.4 million in 2024
audit_findings.mechanism: Any recurring maintenance or deficit-support contribution is an owner cash requirement outside property-and-equipment capex and should reduce OE supporting the equity-method earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: During the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, we made additional equity contributions of $ 20.5 million and $ 1.4 million, respectively, to Arizona Diagnostic Radiology Group ("ADRG", our joint venture with Dignity Health).
audit_findings.explanation: The cash contributions are demonstrated, but their economic character is unresolved. The 2025 amount equals 36.9% of the absolute $55.6 million OE anchor, so a recurring support component could materially reduce value. The sharp increase from $1.4 million in 2024 also leaves open the possibility that much of the contribution funded growth rather than maintenance.
audit_findings.action: Obtain ADRG capital calls, budgets and use-of-funds records; classify each contribution as maintenance, deficit support or growth, reconcile earnings and distributions, and rerun OE after deducting only the recurring maintenance or support component.

audit_findings.title: FY2023 was excluded for a charge that demonstrably recurs
audit_findings.magnitude: $5.146 million FY2023 charge; $0 direct effect on the current $55.6 million latest-actual anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Restoring FY2023 changes the historical OE record and trend diagnostics, but the stated method uses FY2025 latest actual rather than a historical trend for the operating-value anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: During the years ended 2025 2024, and 2023, we experienced lower utilization at various imaging centers which resulted in the closure of these locations and the recognition of lease abandonment charges of approximately $ 8.6 million, $ 2.5 million and $ 5.1 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively, in our Imaging Center segment.
audit_findings.explanation: Excluding the entire year because of an allegedly one-off closure charge is a demonstrated historical-record error: comparable charges were $5.1 million in 2023, $2.5 million in 2024 and $8.6 million in 2025. It is not material to the current scenario values because the model explicitly anchors to FY2025 latest actual, so adding an earlier year cannot change the $55.6 million anchor under the stated method.
audit_findings.action: Restore FY2023, retain unavoidable closure cash costs, add back only verified noncash impairment components, and recompute historical diagnostics; no scenario rerun is needed unless the restored series changes the prescribed anchor-selection rule.
